issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define N[λ] as the integer-valued thinned jump measure with predictable compensator λ_s(dy,X_{s-})ds, using the auxiliary-mark construction already supplied. Impose Poisson independence only on the underlying unthinned measure.
issues.overall_effect: The stochastic representation invokes an incompatible random-measure definition; the same defect affects the preceding discrete and continuous-state jump descriptions.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We set $\gU = C^\infty(\R^d) \cap C^{2,0}(\R^d)$, and $\gV = \gS(\R^d)$, the Schwartz space on $\R^d$.

issues.failure_explanation: Bounding derivatives only through order two does not make a smooth function a multiplier of Schwartz space. In one dimension, f(x)=e^{-3x²}sin(e^{x²}) is smooth with bounded derivatives through order two, and g(x)=e^{-x²} is Schwartz. Their product has high derivatives growing exponentially and is not Schwartz.

failure_location.quote: It is also checked that for any $g \in \gV$, $g \gU \subset \gV$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use an algebra of Schwartz multipliers, for example smooth functions with all derivatives bounded, and impose the corresponding regularity on the functions used in products.
issues.overall_effect: The stated verification of the module condition in ass:V fails, so the ensuing domain justification for Lévy adjoint products is incomplete.
issues.title: The selected Lévy test algebra does not preserve Schwartz functions
